customManagers.description: Home Assistant add-on base images anywhere they're pinned: Dockerfile FROM/ARG lines, workflow ADDON_BASE_IMAGE/HA_IMAGE env vars, and ADDON_BASE_IMAGE constants in integration conftests. A single manager across all three file types so a base-image bump moves every reference together in one PR (the alternative — separate per-file managers or relying on the built-in dockerfile manager for FROM + inline ``# renovate:`` annotations for the rest — split the bumps across two PRs and stranded one set when the other was merged).

Upstream Signal K server base image pinned in the signalk Dockerfile (ARG BUILD_FROM default) -- the single source for the base version (the add-on has no build.yaml; the e2e and CI build from this default). It lives on docker.io, so it falls outside the ghcr.io/home-assistant manager above and needs its own matcher to stay current.
GitHub runner versions in shell scripts and YAML within workflows
Renovate npm package version pinned in CI workflows
Pinned ffmpeg apt package in the integration-test workflow

APK packages pinned in Alpine 3.24 Dockerfiles. Version lookups go through a custom datasource that reads Alpine's own APKINDEX for the pinned suites and returns a Renovate-shaped release list. Replaces the previous Repology datasource (see #6).

home-assistant/builder build-image action (calver-tagged sub-path). Versioning is explicitly 'loose' so the calver tags (2026.06.0) compare correctly — the helpers:pinGitHubActionDigestsToSemver preset would otherwise apply semver to this depName globally, which silently ignores calver and surfaces the old pre-calver semver tags (4.x, 7.x) as 'latest' (cf. closed PRs #246 / #248).
frenck/action-addon-linter schema URLs in pre-commit config

npm packages pinned via pre-commit additional_dependencies (e.g. @commitlint/config-conventional@N in .pre-commit-config.yaml). The built-in pre-commit manager only bumps the `rev:` on each hook — it doesn't touch the additional_dependencies array. Standardized permissive form matches both @scoped and unscoped packages across all sibling repos.
uv tool required-version pin in pyproject.toml [tool.uv]

packageRules.description: ffmpeg apt package resolves from the Ubuntu 24.04 (noble) universe archive, matching the GitHub runner's sources
igt-gpu-tools comes from Alpine edge (master branch of aports), not the 3.24-stable branch. The proxy tries main → community → testing under whichever branch we point at.
onevpl-intel-gpu comes from Alpine edge (master branch of aports), not the 3.24-stable branch.

Avoid duplicate PRs: the custom regex manager above already handles ghcr.io/home-assistant/* FROM lines in Dockerfiles; disabling the built-in dockerfile manager for those packages keeps the regex manager as the single source so we don't get two PRs (one per datasource) on every base-image bump. The /.../ matchPackageNames is regex syntax matching any package name containing 'home-assistant' — the dockerfile manager only sees image names, so this can only hit the HA base images.
Hold CI Python on the 3.14 line to match the Alpine 3.24 base image runtime (python3=3.14.5-r0)

Override the helpers:pinGitHubActionDigestsToSemver preset's semver versioning for home-assistant/builder, which moved from semver tags (1.x-7.x) to calver tags (2026.06.0+). With semver versioning, the calver tags don't parse and Renovate proposes 'upgrades' to the old pre-calver semver tags (this surfaced as the bogus #246 and #248 PRs).

signalk/signalk-server publishes noisy rolling tags (latest-alpine, master-<major>-alpine, sha-<hash>-alpine, <major>-alpine) alongside its v<semver>-alpine releases. Restrict Renovate to the release tags so it tracks real versions and never proposes a rolling or bogus-major 'upgrade'.
